text: Halbrook Regional Health Group provides hospital care to about 2.1 million people across the north of England. The group was founded in 1998 and its registered office is in Wexcombe. It runs six hospitals with a combined 1,616 beds and one rehabilitation clinic in Germany, Halbrook Rehabilitation GmbH. The group is a charitable organisation and any surplus is reinvested in patient services.
header: [Halbrook Regional Health Group Annual Report 2025 | p3 | text: About the group]

text:
Alderbank General Hospital is an acute teaching hospital with 612 beds. Bed occupancy at Alderbank General Hospital averaged 91.3% in 2025.

St Wystan's Hospital is an acute district hospital with 430 beds. Bed occupancy at St Wystan's Hospital averaged 88.7% in 2025.

Pennine Orthopaedic Centre is an elective surgery centre with 148 beds. Bed occupancy at Pennine Orthopaedic Centre averaged 94.0% in 2025.

Marrowdene Community Hospital is a community hospital with 96 beds. Bed occupancy at Marrowdene Community Hospital averaged 82.5% in 2025.

Quillfield Women's and Children's Hospital is a specialist hospital with 210 beds. Bed occupancy at Quillfield Women's and Children's Hospital averaged 85.9% in 2025.

Brackenmoor Mental Health Unit is an inpatient mental health unit with 120 beds. Bed occupancy at Brackenmoor Mental Health Unit averaged 89.2% in 2025.
header: [Halbrook Regional Health Group Annual Report 2025 | p3 | text: Our hospitals]

text:
Four values guide the organisation: respect for every patient, safety before speed, openness about mistakes and the wise use of public money. Each hospital reports against them every quarter, and the programme of colour-coded wristbands introduced in 2023 now covers all inpatient wards.

The group employs 17,940 colleagues. Its largest single site is Alderbank General Hospital, which also hosts the medical school's clinical teaching programme. Pennine Orthopaedic Centre carries out most of the group's elective hip and knee replacements, while Quillfield Women's and Children's Hospital delivers about 9,800 babies a year.

Marrowdene Community Hospital provides rehabilitation beds, a minor injuries unit and outpatient clinics for a rural population. Brackenmoor Mental Health Unit offers acute and rehabilitation care for adults and works closely with community teams in four local authority areas.
header: [Halbrook Regional Health Group Annual Report 2025 | p3 | text: Our values]

text:
Dear colleagues and partners,

2025 was a year of recovery and delivery for the group. Income rose to 1,284.6 million pounds, an increase of 6.9% on the 1,201.3 million recorded in 2024, and we achieved an operating surplus of 23.4 million pounds against 18.9 million pounds the year before. The net surplus was 14.8 million pounds.

Our most important financial achievement was to bring down the cost of temporary staffing. Spending on agency staff fell by 22.4% to 61.2 million pounds, because more of our vacancies were filled by permanent colleagues and because the new staff bank offered flexible shifts at fair rates. The money saved was used to open additional beds and to extend evening clinics.

Capital expenditure reached 96.4 million pounds, up from 71.0 million pounds in 2024. The largest projects were the new theatre complex at Pennine Orthopaedic Centre, which opened on schedule in the autumn, the

rebuilding of the emergency department at St Wystan's Hospital and the replacement of the MRI scanners at Alderbank General Hospital. Each is described in the capital programme table later in this report.
header: [Halbrook Regional Health Group Annual Report 2025 | p4 | text: Chair's review]

text:
The board spent considerable time on safety. We recorded two never events in 2025, one fewer than in 2024, and we continue to treat every one of them as a failure of the system, not of an individual. I would like to thank every colleague for the care they gave, often under heavy pressure, during the winter months.

There were changes in the boardroom. Prof. Anselm Okoro joined as a non-executive director and Sunniva Berg was reappointed for a second term. On behalf of the board I thank Ravi Thandani and his executive team for their leadership throughout the year.

Dr Imogen Falk, Chair
header: [Halbrook Regional Health Group Annual Report 2025 | p4 | text: Chair's review]

text: I am pleased to report that patients waited less time for planned treatment in 2025 than in any of the last five years. The median wait for elective treatment fell to 11.2 weeks at the end of December, compared with 18.1 weeks at the end of 2024.
header: [Halbrook Regional Health Group Annual Report 2025 | p5 | text: Chief executive's report]

text:
Pennine Orthopaedic Centre completed 11.2 thousand

elective procedures. The opening of its new theatre complex gave us four additional operating theatres. Because the complex is also used for day cases from St Wystan's, the number of patients waiting more than eighteen months for a joint replacement fell to zero before the end of the year, which is a first for the group since records began in 2009. The group also reduced the proportion of operations cancelled on the day for non-clinical reasons to 1.9%.
header: [Halbrook Regional Health Group Annual Report 2025 | p5 | text: Planned care]

text: Emergency departments across the group saw 110.9 thousand emergency admissions in 2025. The rebuilt emergency department at St Wystan's will open in 2026 and is expected to reduce the time ambulances spend waiting outside by about a third. In the meantime we opened a same-day emergency care unit at Alderbank General Hospital that treats patients who would otherwise be admitted overnight, and the average length of stay on its medical wards fell by a further two tenths of a day.
header: [Halbrook Regional Health Group Annual Report 2025 | p5 | text: Urgent and emergency care]

text:
The electronic records programme moved from design to delivery. St Wystan's and Marrowdene went live in November and the programme is on budget. The remaining hospitals follow in 2026 and 2027. We have also invested in cyber security after the national alerts of the spring, and we passed an external penetration test in the autumn.

Ravi Thandani, Chief Executive
header: [Halbrook Regional Health Group Annual Report 2025 | p5 | text: Digital]

text: Patient safety is the first priority of our organization. In 2025 the group reported two never events, compared with three in 2024. A never event is a serious incident that is wholly preventable. Both events were investigated by an independent panel and the program of staff training that followed has been completed in all six hospitals.
header: [Halbrook Regional Health Group Annual Report 2025 | p6 | text: Clinical quality]

text:
Hand hygiene audits showed compliance of 97% across all wards. The group recorded 38 cases of MRSA bloodstream infection or Clostridioides difficile attributed to its hospitals, against a ceiling of 46. Our

Safer Wards program uses a color-coded checklist at the bedside so that a nurse can see within seconds which precautions apply to a patient.
header: [Halbrook Regional Health Group Annual Report 2025 | p6 | text: Infection prevention]

text: Medication incidents that reached a patient fell to 3.2 per 1,000 bed days. The pharmacy teams at Alderbank General and St Wystan's introduced barcode scanning at the bedside and plan to extend it to the three smaller hospitals. A review of high-risk drugs found that insulin and anticoagulants account for almost half of all harm from medication.
header: [Halbrook Regional Health Group Annual Report 2025 | p6 | text: Medication safety]

text: The hospital standardized mortality ratio for the group was 0.97, which means that fewer patients died than would be expected given the severity of their conditions. The ratio was 1.02 in 2024. The rate of inpatient falls fell to 4.6 per 1,000 bed days from 5.1, and hospital-acquired pressure ulcers fell by 14% to 212 cases.
header: [Halbrook Regional Health Group Annual Report 2025 | p6 | text: Mortality and harm]

text: The group completed 214 clinical audits in 2025. Of these, 176 reported that practice met the standard set by the relevant professional body, 31 found that improvement was needed and 7 found serious shortcomings that were escalated to the board's quality committee.
header: [Halbrook Regional Health Group Annual Report 2025 | p6 | text: Clinical audit]

text:
More patients told us what they thought of their care. The response rate to the annual patient survey rose from 31% to 38%, the highest since the survey began. Overall, 91% of respondents rated their care as good or very good, and 94% said they would recommend the hospital to family and friends.

At Alderbank General Hospital, 92% of respondents rated their care as good or very good. Patients praised the friendliness of staff and the cleanliness of the building. The most common complaint concerned waiting times for the first appointment.

At St Wystan's Hospital, 90% of respondents rated their care as good or very good. Patients praised the friendliness of staff and the cleanliness of the building. The most common complaint concerned waiting times for the first appointment.

At Pennine Orthopaedic Centre, 96% of respondents rated their care as good or very good. Patients praised the friendliness of staff and the cleanliness of the building. The most common complaint concerned waiting times for the first appointment.

At Marrowdene Community Hospital, 93% of respondents rated their care as good or very good. Patients praised the friendliness of staff and the cleanliness of the building. The most common complaint concerned waiting times for the first appointment.
header: [Halbrook Regional Health Group Annual Report 2025 | p7 | text: Patient experience]

text:
At Quillfield Women's and Children's Hospital, 95% of respondents rated their care as good or very good. Patients praised the friendliness of staff and the cleanliness of the building. The most common complaint concerned waiting times for the first appointment.

At Brackenmoor Mental Health Unit, 84% of respondents rated their care as good or very good. Patients praised the friendliness of staff and the cleanliness of the building. The most common complaint concerned waiting times for the first appointment.
header: [Halbrook Regional Health Group Annual Report 2025 | p7 | text: Patient experience]

text:
The group received 1,142 formal complaints in 2025, down from 1,287 in 2024. The median time to resolve a complaint was 19 working days, within the target of 25. About one complaint in five was upheld in full. We now publish a short summary of lessons learned on every ward, and nurses read it at the start of each shift.

A volunteer program of 1,350 people supports patients at all six hospitals. Volunteers help patients find their way around, read to older patients and run the hospital radio station at Marrowdene.
header: [Halbrook Regional Health Group Annual Report 2025 | p7 | text: Complaints]

text: At the end of 2025 the group employed 17,940 colleagues¹, an increase of 4.1% on the previous year. This is equal to 15,210 whole-time equivalent posts. Nursing and midwifery staff are the largest group, followed by support services and allied health professionals.
header: [Halbrook Regional Health Group Annual Report 2025 | p8 | text: Our people]

text:
Staff costs rose to 782.1 million pounds. A national pay award of 5.5% took effect in April. The group also introduced a cost of living support payment of 300 pounds for colleagues on the lowest pay bands. Gender pay data shows that women are paid on average 14.2% less than men per hour, mostly because they are under-represented in senior medical posts.

Staff turnover fell from 13.4% to 11.8%, and sickness absence from 4.9% to 4.4%. The vacancy rate for registered nurses stood at 7.9% at the year end, down from 10.2%. Our international recruitment programme welcomed 212 nurses from overseas, most of whom joined Alderbank General Hospital and St Wystan's.
header: [Halbrook Regional Health Group Annual Report 2025 | p8 | text: Pay and reward]

text: More than 4,000 colleagues used the confidential counselling service. Each hospital now has a wellbeing champion on every ward, and the quiet rooms opened in 2024 are used, on average, by about 600 colleagues a month.
header: [Halbrook Regional Health Group Annual Report 2025 | p8 | text: Wellbeing]

text: Every new colleague completes a three-day induction. Mandatory training compliance averaged 93%, against a target of 90%. The group trained 148 apprentices, about twice as many as in 2022, and opened a clinical simulation centre at Alderbank General Hospital.
header: [Halbrook Regional Health Group Annual Report 2025 | p8 | text: Training and development]

Cash at the year end stood at 142.7 million pounds, an increase of 22.4 million pounds. The group has agreed a revolving credit facility of 75 million pounds, which was undrawn at the year end.

Drug and energy costs were the main sources of pressure. Spending on drugs rose by 8.3% and the energy bill by 11.0%, although the group has fixed 70% of its gas and electricity requirement for 2026 at lower prices than those paid in 2025.

text:
The accounts have been prepared in accordance with the accounting manual issued for the sector and on the going concern basis. Amounts are stated in pounds sterling, rounded to the nearest hundred thousand pounds, unless otherwise indicated.

Property, plant and equipment is stated at cost less depreciation. Buildings are depreciated over 40 years. Medical and other equipment is depreciated over 5 to 10 years according to its expected useful life. Assets under construction are not depreciated until they are brought into use. Leased assets are depreciated over the shorter of the lease term and their useful life, which is normally 3 to 5 years.
header: [Halbrook Regional Health Group Annual Report 2025 | p19 | text: Note 1: Accounting policies]

text:
Income from patient care activities was 1,168.9 million pounds, or 91.0% of the total. The remainder was education and training (58.3 million pounds), research (21.7 million pounds), and other operating income (35.7 million pounds). Income from the commissioner for the Alderbank region was 612.4 million pounds, which is the largest single source of funds.

Income is recognised when the service is provided. Payments received in advance for training contracts are held as deferred income and released as the training is delivered. At the year end deferred income amounted to 12.6 million pounds².

section: Note 9: Events after the reporting period
text: No adjusting events have occurred since the year end. On 12 February 2026 the board approved a business case for the replacement of the pharmacy robots at Alderbank General Hospital at a cost of 6.2 million pounds. The expenditure will be incurred in 2026 and does not affect the 2025 accounts.

Agency staff Temporary workers supplied by an external employer, used to fill gaps in rotas.

Bed occupancy The share of available beds that are filled by patients, averaged over the year.

Case mix The mixture of patients treated by a hospital, grouped by the complexity of their conditions.

Day case A patient who is admitted for treatment and goes home on the same day without staying overnight.

EBITDA Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation, used here for the German subsidiary.

Length of stay The average number of nights a patient spends in

hospital between admission and discharge.

Never event A serious patient-safety incident that is wholly preventable because national guidance exists to stop it.

Referral to treatment The time between a patient's referral by their doctor and the start of treatment.

Standardized mortality ratio Actual deaths divided by the number expected given the patients' conditions; below 1.00 is better than expected.

Whole-time equivalent A measure of staffing in which one full-time post counts as 1.0, and a half-time post as 0.5.

text:
Workforce availability. The residual rating of this risk at the year end was high. The risk is driven mainly by recruitment of nurses and the use of agency staff. The executive owner reports on mitigation to the audit committee every quarter, and the board reviews it twice a year.

Cyber security. The residual rating of this risk at the year end was high. The risk is driven mainly by the electronic records programme and ageing medical devices. The executive owner reports on mitigation to the audit committee every quarter, and the board reviews it twice a year.

Capital delivery. The residual rating of this risk at the year end was medium. The risk is driven mainly by the emergency department rebuild and the diagnostic hub. The executive owner reports on mitigation to the audit committee every quarter, and the board reviews it twice a year.

Clinical safety. The residual rating of this risk at the year end was medium. The risk is driven mainly by never events and medication errors. The executive owner reports on mitigation to the audit committee every quarter, and the board reviews it twice a year.
header: [Halbrook Regional Health Group Annual Report 2025 | p24 | text: Principal risks]

text:
Regulatory compliance. The residual rating of this risk at the year end was low. The risk is driven mainly by inspection outcomes and registration conditions. The executive owner reports on mitigation to the audit committee every quarter, and the board reviews it twice a year.

Financial resilience. The residual rating of this risk at the year end was medium. The risk is driven mainly by inflation in drug and energy costs. The executive owner reports on mitigation to the audit committee every quarter, and the board reviews it twice a year.

text:
For 2026 we expect income growth of 5% to 6% and capital expenditure of about 110 million pounds, most of it on the emergency department at St Wystan's, the neonatal unit at Quillfield and the electronic records programme. The emergency department will open in the second half of the year.

Quillfield Women's and Children's Hospital will add six neonatal cots when the new unit opens, bringing the total to 24. The maternity unit at Quillfield remained open throughout 2025 and there are no plans to close it.

We do not plan to open a second clinic in Germany. Our focus abroad is on raising the occupancy of the existing one. At home, options for Brackenmoor

Mental Health Unit are under review; we will consult staff and patients before any decision is taken.

The principal uncertainties are the pay award for 2026, the price of energy and the speed at which the delayed diagnostic hub at Marrowdene can be recovered. The group will publish its operating plan once the national funding settlement is confirmed.

Our priorities are to cut the median elective wait below ten weeks, to reduce agency spend again and to complete the roll-out of the electronic records programme to the remaining hospitals. The pension scheme valuation is explained in Appendix D.
header: [Halbrook Regional Health Group Annual Report 2025 | p26 | text: Outlook for 2026]

text: The group used 241,300 MWh of energy in 2025, 3.6% less than in 2024. Carbon emissions from energy use fell to 58.4 thousand tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, from 63.1 thousand tonnes. About 41% of our electricity now comes from renewable sources, and the group has signed a ten-year supply contract with a wind farm in the north of England.
header: [Halbrook Regional Health Group Annual Report 2025 | p27 | text: Sustainability]

text: The group generated 11,800 tonnes of waste, of which 46% was recycled. Single-use plastic in catering was reduced by a third. Clinical waste, which must be incinerated, rose by 2% in line with activity. We plan to replace single-use surgical gowns with reusable ones at Pennine Orthopaedic Centre in 2026.
header: [Halbrook Regional Health Group Annual Report 2025 | p27 | text: Waste]
